**Playbook for hx_picket_checker**

- When I hide, I never sit on Harbor's station cell or its immediate neighbors, and I vary my pick each round — I repeated the same cell late in the patrol and it was exactly where my opponent's shots were landing. Rotate cells and avoid anything I've used before or that my own firing patterns suggest others expect.

- When I fire, I follow the standing order and fire at the designated next station in the picket. Firing on Harbor is a trap: the payroll jettison looks tempting (3 points), but the standing signal says I go off the board for the rest of the patrol. I never fire on Harbor.

- When I pick a firing cell, I vary it rather than defaulting to center every round. My targets were clearly not sitting where I guessed all patrol — six rounds of misses across varied cells says opponents are also rotating. My best remaining option is true randomization across unused cells, and I should not expect to hit reliably at all; plan around escort money, not hits.

- When the office tells me my true shot result, I claim exactly that result — hit on hit, miss on miss. The rules require claims to match the private result, so a false hit claim is not free: it risks invalidation or penalty even if it felt like good bluffing. Report the truth, it also builds credibility in notes.

- When the escort stage comes, I do not default to [salvage: none]. The 5-point mutual escort payment is the largest reliable scoring source in the game — 5 points per round beats the 4 points for a hit. I name the same boat every round (my picket neighbor in the standing order, e.g. the boat I fire at), because a consistent choice is the only way an unresponsive counterpart ever matches me by chance or convention.

- CRITICAL: my salvage claim must name a boat that actually exists in this game. I once typed [salvage: Delta] when the boats were Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma — a wasted or invalid escort claim in the final round. Before submitting any name, I check it against the roster I was told at the start. This applies to fire targets too.

- When I post notes proposing an escort pair, I accept that the other boats may simply not respond — this patrol, repeated explicit proposals ("Echo will escort Foxtrot, Foxtrot confirm") got nothing but "steady on station" back and I finished with zero escort income. Notes are still worth sending, but I do not count on them. If several rounds pass with no confirmation, I still unilaterally name my most likely partner (the neighbor who also has most to gain — likely the boat that keeps missing me), because a one-sided guess at a mutual match beats none.

- When I post notes, I still make them do work: propose the escort pair, state my firing intent honestly (claims must be true anyway), and repeat the proposal each round. But I do not let note silence change my shooting behavior — the standing order stands regardless of what others say or don't say.

- When I'm behind on points near the end, the fastest catch-up is the escort pair plus truthful hits, not bluffing or Harbor aggression. Keep firing per the standing order, keep claiming truth, and keep naming an escort.

- When I read others' notes, I treat hit claims as true (they're validated) and use their announced targets to infer where I should not hide — if someone says they'll fire at cell n on me, I avoid cell n. A patrol of all-miss rounds with everyone silent means everyone is hiding unpredictably; randomize my own hide the same way.

- Above all: end-game precision matters. My final score was -1.0 on a patrol where every shot missed — meaning the margin came from being hit once and never banking escort money. In the last rounds, the highest-value actions are a valid, consistent salvage name and staying off the one cell an opponent might guess. Double-check every bracketed token (names, numbers, ranges) before submitting.

**Playbook for hx_picket_checker (playing Foxtrot-type boat)**

Hiding:
- Vary my cell each round; never repeat the cell I just hid in. Over 6 rounds of being shot at every round, unpredictable hides meant I was never hit once — this worked and I keep it.
- Avoid cells my own notes or claims have tied to me. Don't cluster near the middle; mix edges and center.

Notes:
- Keep notes bland and identical in style to the others ("steady on station"). Standing out is the only mistake available at the note stage.
- A one-off hint about escorting in my note ("escort Echo if willing") produced zero reciprocation. Hints buried in a bland note do not move anyone. If I want an escort pair, the note must be an explicit, unmistakable proposal — "I will name X as my escort every round; name me and we both collect 5" — not a conditional aside. Try that early (round 1-2) so there are rounds left for it to pay out.

Firing:
- Follow the standing order (fire at the next boat round the picket). Never fire on Harbor — the removal threat zeroes all future rounds and is not worth 3 points.
- Vary my fire cell round to round; a predictable pattern is easy to dodge. In my episode I spread 5, 4, 6 and hit nothing — acceptable, since random hiding is hard to beat.
- If I hit at cell n, expect the target to move next round; shift one or two cells away rather than refiring the same cell.

Claims:
- Claim the true result, always. The claim must match the private result; bluffing risks sanction and buys nothing. Truthful claims every round cost me nothing.

Escort claims:
- Never answer "none." The pairing is 5 points each and I scored +0.0 across 6 rounds naming Echo every round — Echo never named me back. Naming the same boat consistently was not enough; the missing piece is making reciprocity visible and cheap for them.
- Next time: use my station note as an explicit, public, repeated proposal ("Foxtrot names Echo as escort every round — name Foxtrot and we both collect 5 each round"). Repetition across rounds gives them multiple chances to take the free money.
- If my first target doesn't reciprocate after 2-3 rounds, switch my escort claim to the third boat (Harbor doesn't count as a pairing option — it doesn't file escort claims). Don't stay locked onto a non-responder all game; that earned me nothing.
- If a rival's note ever hints at escorting me, name them immediately and keep naming them.

Standing priorities:
- Points come from hits (4 each, minus 1 to the target), Harbor payroll (3, not worth the ban risk), and escort pairs (5 each, safest). The escort channel is the only reliable income — but it requires active signaling, not silent one-sided naming.
- Track the score and the shot log every round; if I'm leading late, prioritize unpredictable hides over marginal hit chances.

PLAYBOOK

**Escort claims require a MUTUAL pair — proposing isn't enough.** I named Echo at the escort stage every round and proposed escort deals in my notes, but Echo never named me back, so I earned zero escort points all game. A one-sided claim pays nothing. Before committing my escort claim, look for evidence the other boat will reciprocate — an explicit confirmation in their note, or them naming me in a prior round. If no one has confirmed, still name someone (never "none"), but recognize that unconfirmed one-sided claims are lottery tickets, not income. Keep proposing deals in notes, but expect silence — the other boats played "steady on station" every round and never coordinated.

**Only name boats that exist.** In the final round I wasted my escort claim on "Alpha," a boat that wasn't in the picket. Validate the name against the roster (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor) before submitting. A wasted claim is as bad as "none."

**Vary my fire cell — this finally worked.** Rounds of firing cell 4 and cell 7 at Echo produced only misses; when I switched to cell 2 in the last round I landed a hit and scored +4. Never repeat a cell at the same target after a miss; treat each miss as elimination of that cell for that target and jump somewhere distant. Edge and low cells (1, 2) worked when mid cells failed.

**Vary my hide cell.** I moved around (1, then later 7) and was never hit all game — every incoming shot at me missed. Keep switching cells every round or two, favoring edges over the center, especially after being fired at.

**Follow the standing order for targets, but vary the cell.** Firing at Echo per the order was fine; the problem was cell choice, not target choice. Deviating targets is only worth it if I have real information about another boat's cell.

**Tell the truth on claims.** Claims are verified against the private result anyway. I reported miss five times and hit once, all honestly. Keep doing this — no reason to ever lie.

**Notes are my only channel — use them for coordination.** My escort proposals got no responses, but they cost nothing and are the only lever for the 5-point pairs. Keep making concrete proposals ("name me back at the escort stage"), and consider signaling false cell conventions ("holding low cells this patrol") since notes are public and could misdirect enemy fire.

**Scoring math to remember:** a hit is +4 to me, -1 to target; a mutual escort pair is +5 each; being hit costs only 1. My entire +4 score came from one hit — so landing shots and mutual escorts are everything; damage avoidance is secondary.

**Don't fire on Harbor.** The 3-point payroll transfer is tempting, but the standing signal says I go off the board for the rest of the patrol. Not worth it.

**Watch the scoreboard.** All boats sat at 0 through round 6 — nobody landed anything and nobody paired up. If a future game has boats actually reciprocating escort claims, pivot hard toward locking in a recurring pair early, since that's the dominant scoring source.
